justification: Inspected byte-buddy-dep/src/main/java/net/bytebuddy/implementation/attribute/MethodAttributeAppender.java (lines 244-405) and byte-buddy-dep/src/test/java/net/bytebuddy/implementation/attribute/MethodAttributeAppenderExplicitTest.java (lines 45-163). Explicit is about 160 lines with 2 public constructors, 3 static factory helpers, make/apply, and a small nested Target abstraction with only two implementations (method vs parameter); all of it serves one cohesive task: writing explicit annotations to a method or one parameter. The tests exercise the same single concern (method annotations, parameter annotations, and parameter-index validation), and I did not see separate, low-cohesion responsibilities that would justify splitting the class.
